title: Switzerland – Electrical installation work – PWA-T3, T5, T6 (Selektiv) Ausschreibung Elektro, BKP 232 Niederspannungsinstallationen
description: Die Infrastruktur des Flughafens Zürich unterliegt einem schrittweisen Erneuerungsprozess. In den letzten 15 Jahren sind verschiedene Teile der zentralen Flughafeninfrastruktur umfassend saniert und erweitert worden: Das Dock B wurde komplett umgebaut, der Terminal 2 totalsaniert und erweitert, und zwischen den Terminal 1 und 2 wurde das neue Sicherheitskontrollgebäude mit zentralisiertem Zugang in das Airside Center erstellt. Derzeit werden die zentrale Gepäcksortieranlage nördlich des Terminal 1 erweitert und das flughafenweite Gepäcksortiersystem abgelöst und erneuert. In einem nächsten Schritt müssen die in die Jahre gekommenen Teile der zentralen Flughafen- Infrastruktur ersetzt werden: Das Dock A wurde zusammen mit dem Tower 1985 in Betrieb genommen und blieb in seiner Struktur bis heute weitgehend unverändert. Bezüglich Funktionalität, Nachhaltigkeit und Qualität kann das Dock A die heutigen Anforderungen nicht mehr erfüllen. Aufgrund einer umfassenden Analyse wurde entschieden, das bestehende Dock A durch einen Neubau nördlich des heutigen Gebäudes zu ersetzen. Der Ersatzneubau für das Dock A, der neue Tower und das umfassend sanierte Vorfeld zum Dock A mit allen weiteren Anpassungen, Erweiterungen und Umbauten der zentralen Flughafeninfrastruktur sind die sichtbar wichtigsten baulichen Massnahmen der nächsten 15 bis 20 Jahre. Bei der etappenweisen Realisierung muss gewährleistet werden, dass der Betrieb normal weitergeführt werden kann und mit den neu erstellten Gebäuden die künftigen funktionalen Anforderungen erfüllt werden können. Das Projekt PWA.T «Perimeterfreilegung Wurzel A» ist in drei Teilprojekte (T3, T5 und T6) unterteil und beinhaltet die Umsetzung von Anpassungen an bestehenden Medien und Anlagen. Diese befinden sich im und auch ausserhalb des Abbruchsperimeters der Wurzel Dock A. Die Arbeiten sind für den Bauzustand des Rückbaus und für die weiteren Phasen des Hauptprojekts Luftseite zu realisieren. Die Ausführung der vorliegenden Leistungen beginnt bereits 2027 und erfolgt etappiert; der Schwerpunkt liegt gemäss den indikativen Projektterminen (Kapitel IV, Ziffer 1.1) in den Jahren 2027 bis 2029. Nachgelagerte Etappen im Zusammenhang mit dem Hauptprojekt Luftseite können nach einer längeren Unterbrechung bis ca. 2033 folgen. Diese späten Termine dienen lediglich der Orientierung; sie entsprechen dem aktuellen Planungsstand und können sich im weiteren Projektverlauf ändern. Im Abbruchperimeter der Dockwurzel A sind essenzielle Teile der Gebäudetechnik für die Versorgung des Kontroll-Towers, Dockwurzel A, Dock A, Airside Center und der Passkontrollhalle verortet.

title: Denmark – Construction work – Udbud af ret til at virke som ladeoperatør af offentligt tilgængelige ladepunkter i Gentofte Kommune (Genudbud)
description: Dette udbud vedrører Gentofte Kommunens overladelse af retten til at virke som operatør af offent-ligt tilgængelige ladepunkter på kommunale vejarealer i Gentofte Kommune jf. Europa-parlamentets og Rådets forordning 203/1804 af 13. september 2023 om etablering af infrastruktur for alternative drivmidler og AFI-loven (LBK nr. 1043 af 17/09/2024 Bekendtgørelse af lov om infrastruktur for alternative drivmidler). Udbuddet gennemføres som et koncessionsudbud, jf. Direktiv 2014/23/EU om tildeling af koncessionskontrakter (Koncessionsdirektivet), da den samlede værdi af koncessionen forventes at udgøre DKK 220.000.000, hvilket er over tærskelværdien for EU-udbud (beregnet i overensstemmelse med den i Koncessionsdirektivets artikel 8, stk. 3 angivne metode ved anvendelse af Vejdirektoratets skabelon for beregning af koncessionsværdien). Udbudsmaterialet henviser derudover til LBK nr. 116 af 3. februar 2025, ”Udbudsloven” hvor relevant. Gentofte Kommune (Kommunen) har en eksisterende portefølje af koncessionskontrakter vedrørende retten til at virke som Ladeoperatør med forestående udløb, som derfor skal genudbydes. Derudover har Kommunen behov for at udbyde et antal nye lokationer som følge af øget behov og efterspørgsel på offentligt tilgængelige Ladepunkter i Gentofte Kommune. Udbuddet omfattet i alt 220 Ladepunkter. Af Bilag 3 Lokationsliste fremgår en oversigt over lokationer med angivelse af antal Ladepunkter til etablering på den konkrete lokation. Af Bilag 3 Lokationsliste fremgår det, om der er tale om et genudbud eller en ny-etablering af Ladepunkt. De enkelte lokationer er vurderet egnede ift. trafikale hensyn og placeret, hvor behovet og efterspørgslen vurderes størst. Det samlede antal Lokationer/Ladepunkter der udbydes er fordelt på ni delaftaler. Af Bilag 3 Lokationsliste fremgår, hvilke Lokationer der er omfattet af hvilke delaftaler. Ladeoperatøren har frit valg mht. hvilken type lader (normallader, hurtiglader eller lynlader) der op-stilles på lokationen, typen skal dog fremgå af tilbuddet og angives i Operatørens løsningsbeskrivelse for den enkelte delaftale. Kommunen udbyder alene retten til at virke som Ladeoperatør på de pågældende lokationer. Det er de bydendes opgave at skitsere løsning på de enkelte lokationer, herunder valg af type af lader (normal- hurtig- eller lynlader) samt antal Ladepunkter pr. Ladestander. Operatøren skal selv finansiere omkostningerne til etablering, drift og nedtagning af egne Ladepunkter. Hvor der i dag er etableret et Ladepunkt med udløb af koncessionskontrakt, skal Operatøren koordinere opstilling med den eksisterende operatørs nedtagning. Lokationerne udbydes som individuelle delaftaler. Der kan afgives tilbud på enkelte eller alle delaftaler, men samme tilbudsgiver kan ikke tildeles alle delaftaler, der henvises til afsnit 4.2 for nærmere beskrivelse af tildeling af delaftaler. Der indgås enslydende kontrakter for hver enkelt delaftale. Udbuddet gennemføres efter en proces, der svarer til offentligt udbud, hvor alle egnede leverandø-rer har adgang til at afgive tilbud.

description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products or commercial services prepared in accordance with RFO Part 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. Solicitation Number 70SBUR27R00000004 is issued as a Request for Proposal (RFP) for DHS purchase and maintenance of eight (8) card counters for the United States Citizenship & Immigration Services (USCIS) for the total potential period of performance of 01/01/2027 � 12/31/2031 in accordance with the attached Statement of Work. RFP 70SBUR27R00000004 is being issued with the intent to make one (1) award. Award will be based on the lowest priced technically acceptable basis. Submission of a complete proposal constitutes affirmation of your ability to provide the item and maintenance in accordance with the criteria outlined in the attached solicitation documents. Amendments to this solicitation will be publicized in the same manner as the initial synopsis and solicitation. The Government is requesting maximum additional discounts beyond standard commercial pricing for the requirement. The proposal shall display any discount provided by the contractor and should represent the best possible price that the contractor can provide. description: The Defense Health Agency Contracting Activity (DHACA), Healthcare Contracting Division???????????????????????????San Antonio (HCD-SA), intends to award a firm-fixed-price sole-source contract to Philips North America LLC to provide Raymond W. Bliss Army Health Center, Fort Huachuca, Arizona, with comprehensive maintenance and accidental-damage coverage for the existing Government-owned Philips Digital Diagnost C90 High Performance (HP) X-ray system.Philips Healthcare is the original equipment manufacturer (OEM) of the DigitalDiagnost C90 HP system and possesses the proprietary knowledge, software, diagnostic tools, and hardware necessary to maintain and repair the equipment. Ireland – Railway construction works – TII499 Luas Finglas Main Infrastructure Design and Construction Works
description: Luas Finglas is a 4 km extension of the Luas Green Line, delivering a high-capacity light rail connection between Finglas and Dublin city centre to support sustainable transport and urban development. The scheme will serve communities including Charlestown, Finglas Village, Finglas West, St Helena’s, and the Tolka Valley, and will comprise four new stops at St Helena’s, Finglas Village, St Margaret’s Road, and Charlestown. It also includes a 350-space Park and Ride facility near St Margaret’s Road, as well as interchange opportunities with bus services and with mainline rail services at Broombridge. The Luas Finglas Main Infrastructure Design and Construction Works will be delivered under the NEC4 Engineering and Construction Contract (ECC) Option C (Target Cost with Activity Schedule). The scope of this Contract (TII-499) includes, but is not limited to, the design and construction of the following principal elements: 1. Site clearance and demolitions. 2. Track (trackbed and rails). 3. Luas Stops at St Helena’s, Finglas Village, St Margaret’s Road and Charlestown. 4. Broombridge stabling site works. 5. Park and Ride facilities at St Margaret's Road. 6. Royal canal and rail overbridge at Broombridge. 7. Tolka Valley Park Bridge. 8. Fencing, retaining walls, boundary treatments and accommodation work. 9. Utility services realignment, diversion, replacement, and protection. 10. Road realignments and junction modifications. 11. Pedestrian and cycling facilities including cycle storage structures. 12. Road traffic signalling. 13. Landscape and urban realm upgrades. 14. Overhead Catenary System (OCS). 15. Power and Systems infrastructure. 16. Signalling, controls and other rail systems. 17. Working in live traffic environment on the busiest radial corridors in the greater Dublin area including property and business frontage reconfiguration. 18. Heritage / archaeology mitigation works. 19. Installation of stop furniture. 20. Installation of Validators and Ticket Vending Machines. 21. Other Ancillary works. The successful Contractor will also be responsible for: • Overall systems integration. • Interfacing and co-ordinating with other works packages to facilitate completion of works. • Interfacing and co-ordinating with stakeholders. • Testing and commissioning.

title: Landscaping and Snow Removal USCG TRACEN Cape May
description: THIS IS A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) AND INDUSTRY DAY ANNOUNCEMENT ONLY. This notice is issued solely for market-research and planning purposes. It is not a solicitation, request for proposal, or commitment by the U.S. Coast Guard to award a contract or reimburse respondents for information or costs incurred in responding. The U.S. Coast Guard seeks industry feedback regarding a potential requirement for grounds maintenance, seasonal cleanup, landscaping support, and snow/ice-removal services at the U.S. Coast Guard Training Center (TRACEN) Cape May Family Housing Complex, 1 Munro Avenue, Cape May, New Jersey 08204. TRACEN Cape May maintains approximately 173 Coast Guard-owned family-housing units located in the 1400, 1500, 1600, 1700, and 1800 blocks, along with single-family homes and associated common areas. Common areas include lawns, sidewalks, walkways, parking areas, playgrounds, a basketball court, and bus stops. The anticipated requirement would include all personnel, supervision, equipment, tools, vehicles, materials, supplies, transportation, and incidental services necessary to perform routine grounds maintenance, seasonal cleanup, limited tree and shrub trimming, and snow/ice-removal services. Anticipated services include mowing, edging, trimming, weed removal or treatment, spring cleanup, fall cleanup, snow removal, and ice-control treatment for designated housing and common areas. Unless otherwise identified in the final requirement, services are not anticipated within fenced private backyards. The Government�s objective is to maintain housing-complex grounds, common areas, pedestrian routes, parking areas, and bus stops in a safe, neat, accessible, and usable condition. Routine grounds-maintenance services are anticipated principally during the growing season, generally April through November; snow and ice removal would be required in response to winter-weather events. The Government requests industry feedback on: (1) capability and experience performing comparable services; (2) recommended scope, performance standards, and measurable outcomes; (3) seasonal staffing and equipment approach; (4) snow/ice response times and pricing practices; (5) commercial contract structure and period-of-performance considerations; and (6) small-business capability and interest. Commercial-Service Feedback: The Government seeks information to assess whether the anticipated services are available commercially and whether the draft scope, performance standards, and anticipated terms can be met using customary commercial practices. Industry Day: 12/01/2026 10:00 AM, 1 Munro Ave, Cape May, NJ 08204 at Tennis Court RFI Response Due: 12/03/2026 10:00 AM Point of Contact: Mr. Andrew Haungs, SMB-FORCECOM-042@uscg.mil ATTACHMENTS: 1.Statement of Work-- RFI SOW TCCM Houseing Grounds Maintenance, Seasonal Cleanup, and Snow and Ice Removal 2.TRACEN Cape May Family Housing Service-Area Map 3. title: Landscaping and Snow Removal USCG TRACEN Cape May
description: THIS IS A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) AND INDUSTRY DAY ANNOUNCEMENT ONLY. This notice is issued solely for market-research and planning purposes. It is not a solicitation, request for proposal, or commitment by the U.S. Coast Guard to award a contract or reimburse respondents for information or costs incurred in responding. The U.S. Coast Guard seeks industry feedback regarding a potential requirement for grounds maintenance, seasonal cleanup, landscaping support, and snow/ice-removal services at the U.S. Coast Guard Training Center (TRACEN) Cape May Family Housing Complex, 1 Munro Avenue, Cape May, New Jersey 08204. TRACEN Cape May maintains approximately 173 Coast Guard-owned family-housing units located in the 1400, 1500, 1600, 1700, and 1800 blocks, along with single-family homes and associated common areas. Common areas include lawns, sidewalks, walkways, parking areas, playgrounds, a basketball court, and bus stops. The anticipated requirement would include all personnel, supervision, equipment, tools, vehicles, materials, supplies, transportation, and incidental services necessary to perform routine grounds maintenance, seasonal cleanup, limited tree and shrub trimming, and snow/ice-removal services. Anticipated services include mowing, edging, trimming, weed removal or treatment, spring cleanup, fall cleanup, snow removal, and ice-control treatment for designated housing and common areas. Unless otherwise identified in the final requirement, services are not anticipated within fenced private backyards. The Government�s objective is to maintain housing-complex grounds, common areas, pedestrian routes, parking areas, and bus stops in a safe, neat, accessible, and usable condition. Routine grounds-maintenance services are anticipated principally during the growing season, generally April through November; snow and ice removal would be required in response to winter-weather events. The Government requests industry feedback on: (1) capability and experience performing comparable services; (2) recommended scope, performance standards, and measurable outcomes; (3) seasonal staffing and equipment approach; (4) snow/ice response times and pricing practices; (5) commercial contract structure and period-of-performance considerations; and (6) small-business capability and interest. Commercial-Service Feedback: The Government seeks information to assess whether the anticipated services are available commercially and whether the draft scope, performance standards, and anticipated terms can be met using customary commercial practices. Industry Day: 12/01/2026 10:00 AM, 1 Munro Ave, Cape May, NJ 08204 at Tennis Court RFI Response Due: 12/03/2026 10:00 AM Point of Contact: Mr. Andrew Haungs, SMB-FORCECOM-042@uscg.mil ATTACHMENTS: 1.Statement of Work-- RFI SOW TCCM Houseing Grounds Maintenance, Seasonal Cleanup, and Snow and Ice Removal 2.TRACEN Cape May Family Housing Service-Area Map 3. title: Manchester International Airport Phase 2 - Platform Civils
description: "The planned introduction of longer train services to the Airport in response to future demand growth will mean that double stacking arrangements of trains as currently used will no longer be viable. Through the project's Delivery Steering Group, Northern and TransPennine Express have carried out analysis which has identified that additional platform capacity is needed at the airport in order to realise the full benefit of longer train services serving the airport. The scheme is part of a package of proposed measures in the Manchester area that are being designed/planned to boost capacity and resilience, emanating from the Cross Manchester Capacity and Reliability Improvement Study. Improving the operation of train services in the centre of Manchester and providing further capacity at Manchester Airport station, aligns with the strategic aims of Network Rail, TfGM, TfN and the wider industry. This project in in Tranche 1 of the Manchester and North West Transformation Programme (MNTP): A remodelling of the station at Manchester Airport, specifically a platform addition or extension of multiple platforms, or provision of a new turnback facility, will be essential to accommodate the planned implementation of longer rolling stock services. The redevelopment of these platforms will enable permissive working of two 6x24m (144m) trains, in two of the four platforms at the Airport Station. This will allow for the unaltered retention of all existing TOC services both originating and terminating at the Airport Station under 'double-stacking' conditions. The works comprise the construction and completion of the platform civils work at Manchester Airport Station. • Platform demolition • Asset recoveries • Track walkway/crossings • UTX • Troughing • Riser wall foundations • New riser walls (blockwork and PCC) • Copers (including realignment) • Tactile paving • Drainage (ACO's and carrier) • Ducting • Equipment foundations (in-situ and PCC) • Waiting shelter foundations • Platform furniture • SME works (end of platform ramps) • Fencing/Gate works • Block paving/surfacing • Associated reinstatement works

title: BioWatch Program
description: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) SUMMARY: The Department of Homeland Security (DHS), FEMA, Office of Resilience, Chemical, Biological, Radiological, and Nuclear (CBRN) Support Directorate, requires support to staff identified local field offices and execute the daily BioWatch Program field operations in accordance with the attached Statement of Work (SOW). GENERAL INFORMATION: This RFI is issued solely for information gathering purposes to identify sources that can provide support for the BioWatch program field operations, special events and surge operations, and technology upgrades and integration. In accordance with FAR 15.101(c), RFIs may be used when the Government wants to obtain price, delivery, other market information, and capabilities for planning purposes. Responses to these RFIs are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. This RFI shall not be construed as a commitment by the Government for any purpose, nor does it restrict the Government to an ultimate acquisition approach. Respondents are solely responsible for all expenses associated with their RFI response. Respondents will not receive additional information in response to their submittal to the RFI and will not be notified of the resulting market research. INTRODUCTION: DHS�s mission is to safeguard the American people, the homeland, and American values with honor and integrity. In support of this mission, the FEMA works to prevent CBRN attacks against the United States by providing timely, responsive support to operational partners. The CBRN Support Directorate advances this mission through the BioWatch program, the nation�s only civilian program that monitors for aerosol releases of select bioterrorism agents. Since its establishment in 2003, BioWatch has maintained a bioterrorism air monitoring system that operates 24 hours a day, 7 days a week in large metropolitan areas, known as jurisdictions, and partnered with state and local public health communities to prepare for and respond to bioterrorist events. The BioWatch Program�s strategic objectives are to: Monitor for the highest-priority biological agents that could cause catastrophic outcomes. Protect the nation�s most at-risk locations. Maintain technical oversight of operations in close collaboration with state and local public health partners that execute the program. Conduct advanced development and use federal research and development (R&D) to procure and deploy improved detection capabilities at lower cost. Coordinate federal, state, and local public health preparedness activities to develop operational protocols for initiating response activities following the detection of an agent for which the system tests. Strengthen federal, state, and local stakeholder partnerships and improve operational efficiencies. To accomplish these objectives, each BioWatch jurisdiction maintains a static array of air samplers, the filters of which are collected daily by field operators. These filters are then delivered to a state or local operational laboratory where they are analyzed for select biological agents. Jurisdictions may also elect to surge operations by deploying additional units to monitor special events or increasing the collection cycle (e.g., twice a day collections). In addition, each jurisdiction has an advisory committee that coordinates with the BioWatch program on operations and biological event preparedness activities. At the federal level, the BioWatch program includes field, surge, laboratory, and biodefense preparedness operational components. Figure 1 depicts daily sample operations. Figure 1. BioWatch Sample Operational Process PURPOSE OF RFI Currently field operators and field-related tasks are not staffed by contract. The purpose of this RFI is to evaluate and determine the field staffing and support options for the BioWatch program to meet field operations requirements. The performer must enable the BioWatch program to maintain current field operations and continue to provide high quality, reliable, and timely delivery of field samples to the laboratories. In addition, due to its evolving operational needs, the performer must provide the necessary flexibility and adaptability to ensure BioWatch can address changes in sample collections for both planned events and unforeseen incidents, as well as assist with potential technology assessments, field evaluations, integration, and implementation. DESIRED CAPABILITIES FOR BIOWATCH FIELD STAFFING AND SUPPORT CAPABILITY Competent, proficient, and reliable field staffing is essential to ensure the BioWatch program continues to meet established requirements. In addition, the evolving threats and vulnerabilities that are identified at the state and local level require operational flexibility and adaptability that must be able to be supported with field staff capable of performing field operations and chain of custody in accordance with mission needs. A successful candidate staffing performer will provide field personnel to conduct BioWatch daily operations in select metropolitan cities within the United States. Composition and hierarchy of field staff at each location will be made at the discretion of the performer, with recommendations and concurrence from the BioWatch program. The staffing performer shall: Provide a Program Manager for the contract who will serve as the primary point of contact for the BioWatch Program and DHS Contracting Officer. Provide a primary point of contact, or lead, for each jurisdiction who will provide direct oversight of field staff and be responsible for administrative activities such as: Scheduling field staff and scoping collection routes. Maintaining appropriate documentation (e.g., training documentation, required inventories, etc.) Coordinating delivery times with local BioWatch laboratory. Communicating and coordinating with the BioWatch Field Operations team. Participating in relevant program meetings. Upon request, participating in local advisory committee meetings. Responding to requests for information from the BioWatch program. Supporting program audits and other assessments. Provide local office space to include space for equipment and consumable supplies storage. Implement staff recruitment and retention practices to maintain staffing levels over the life of the contract to: Support routine daily operations 7 days a week, 365 days a year and may require working beyond a standard 8-hour day and/or alternate shifts. Support planned and limited notice special events and surge operations (i.e., equipment deployment/demobilization, increased operations tempo, increased collection cycle, expanded array, etc.). Support changes to the static array (i.e., additions/reductions in number of collection sites) or collection routes. Ensure the staffing level in a given jurisdiction does not fall below 75% for longer than 1 month and that overall staffing levels do not fall below 90% per year. Accommodate appropriate and reasonable time off for personnel (i.e., paid time off, etc.) without compromising operations including special events and surge operations. Provide continuity of operations, which may include: Changes in operational tempo caused by limited notice special events. Travel of field staff from one jurisdiction to another for either surge support or to ensure continued steady-state operations. Perform all required operational tasks in accordance with the Field Operations Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) and other program guidance, processes, and protocols, including: Logistics support. Equipment and supplies ordering and inventory maintenance and reporting. Ensure all field staff, including new hires, are appropriately trained in all relevant BioWatch operations procedures, processes, and protocols. Training materials are provided by the BioWatch program but the performer may be required to develop, maintain, and provide additional training to meet and support program objectives. Ensure field

title: Unison
description: The Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) is soliciting innovative proposals for Unison, a program to develop and evaluate collaborative-autonomy approaches that jointly adapt team decision-making and communications during mission execution. Unison will investigate approaches that enable autonomous teams to modify tactics, behaviors, coordination relationships, and information exchange as mission complexity and operational variability increase and communications become constrained and/or degraded (see Section 7, Glossary, for program-specific definitions of terms in italics). The core hypothesis of Unison is that a unified execution-time reasoning approach to action planning and communications planning can improve the effectiveness, scalability, and resilience of collaborative autonomy in dynamic, uncertain, and resource-constrained environments. Unison seeks to preserve mission performance while reducing communication dependence and bounding the reasoning burden imposed on individual agents. Unison frames collaborative autonomy as a multi-agent decision problem in which agents use local observations, mission context, relevance, and mission objectives to select a policy that jointly defines physical actions and communications actions. At each decision point, the team must determine what actions to take, which coordination relationships must be maintained, and what information must be exchanged to preserve the coordination required for mission success. Unison will investigate approaches across teams of tens to hundreds of agents operating in representative collaborative, multi-domain mission scenarios.

title: PAE Maritime PMS 500 Industry Day Announcement - DDG 1001 Conventional Prompt Strike (CPS) DMP Technical Exchange
description: Industry Day Announcement in support of Naval Sea Systems Command (PAE Maritime). THIS NOTIFICATION IS BEING MADE TO PROVIDE PARTICIPANTS WITH THE MAXIMUM AMOUNT OF TIME FOR SCHEDULING AND MAKING TRAVEL ARRANGEMENTS. The program office for Guided Missile Destroyer (DDG) Zumwalt Class (PMS 500) intends to conduct an Industry Day in Washington, DC, on 9 Dec 2026. This Industry Day will be solely a technical exchange focused on the DDG 1001 Conventional Prompt Strike (CPS) Depot Modernization Period (DMP). PMS 500 is conducting market research and technical dialogue to assess industry capability, technical execution strategies, and industrial capacity specifically in support of the upcoming DDG 1001 CPS DMP requirements. Program Background The DDG 1000 Zumwalt-class guided missile destroyers represent the Navy's premier multi-mission, stealth-oriented surface combatants, designed to deliver decisive long-range precision fires and operational deterrence. The overarching DDG 1000 Class Maintenance and Modernization strategy provides a synchronized, lifecycle framework to maintain class operational readiness, sustain advanced engineering systems, and field next-generation combat capabilities across all class hulls. A foundational element of this class-wide campaign is the incorporation of the Conventional Prompt Strike (CPS) hypersonic weapon system capability on USS MICHAEL MONSOOR (DDG 1001) during her CPS Depot Modernization Period (DMP); May 2028 � Aug 2030. This modernization strategy encompasses: Hypersonic Payload Integration: Large-scale structural modifications, compartment reconfiguration, and integration of the Conventional Prompt Strike (CPS) payload module and specialized launcher infrastructure to field prompt, long-range hypersonic strike capabilities. Combat System & Computing Infrastructure Upgrades: Comprehensive Total Ship Computing Environment Infrastructure (TSCEI) software/hardware modernization, open architecture enhancements, and tactical weapon control interfacing. Power & Thermal Management Expansion: Auxiliary plant enhancements, power conversion and distribution upgrades, and high-efficiency chilled water cooling modifications required to support advanced mission systems and weapon suites. Depot-Level Maintenance & Sustainment: Dry-docking evolutions, hull/mechanical/electrical (HM&E) overhaul, signature-managed hull preservation, and routine depot-level maintenance concurrent with major modernization packages. Within this broader class-wide maintenance and modernization framework, the upcoming DDG 1001 CPS DMP constitutes a critical execution milestone, demanding rigorous advance technical interchange between the Government and prospective industrial base performers to de-risk planning, interfaces, and industrial execution. Industry Day Purpose and Details PMS 500 will host this Industry Day solely as a technical exchange on the DDG 1001 CPS DMP. The primary intent is to engage in focused technical dialogue regarding the specific design, interface, production, schedule, and industrial execution challenges associated with this DMP, as well as to receive feedback from industry to refine technical requirements. PMS 500 will post a Requests For Information (RFI) containing targeted technical questions prior to the event, with the intent to conduct a technical exchange with Industry. PMS 500 is seeking attendance from companies that already possess a current PAE Maritime Master Ship Repair (MSR) Agreement and that demonstrate the technical capability and dry-dock/pier-side infrastructure necessary to execute the specialized industrial scope of the DDG 1001 CPS DMP. Companies that do not already possess a PAE Maritime MSR Agreement may participate if they intend to have such an agreement in place prior to the award and execution of the DMP. Respondents will not receive additional information in response to their submittal to the RFI and will not be notified of the resulting market research. INTRODUCTION: DHS�s mission is to safeguard the American people, the homeland, and American values with honor and integrity. In support of this mission, the FEMA works to prevent CBRN attacks against the United States by providing timely, responsive support to operational partners. The CBRN Support Directorate advances this mission through the BioWatch program, the nation�s only civilian program that monitors for aerosol releases of select bioterrorism agents. Since its establishment in 2003, BioWatch has maintained a bioterrorism air monitoring system that operates 24 hours a day, 7 days a week in large metropolitan areas, known as jurisdictions, and partnered with state and local public health communities to prepare for and respond to bioterrorist events. The BioWatch Program�s strategic objectives are to: Monitor for the highest-priority biological agents that could cause catastrophic outcomes. Protect the nation�s most at-risk locations. Maintain technical oversight of operations in close collaboration with state and local public health partners that execute the program. Conduct advanced development and use federal research and development (R&D) to procure and deploy improved detection capabilities at lower cost. Coordinate federal, state, and local public health preparedness activities to develop operational protocols for initiating response activities following the detection of an agent for which the system tests. Strengthen federal, state, and local stakeholder partnerships and improve operational efficiencies. To accomplish these objectives, each BioWatch jurisdiction maintains a static array of air samplers, the filters of which are collected daily by field operators. These filters are then delivered to a state or local operational laboratory where they are analyzed for select biological agents. Jurisdictions may also elect to surge operations by deploying additional units to monitor special events or increasing the collection cycle (e.g., twice a day collections). In addition, each jurisdiction has an advisory committee that coordinates with the BioWatch program on operations and biological event preparedness activities. A successful candidate staffing performer will provide field personnel to conduct BioWatch daily operations in select metropolitan cities within the United States. Composition and hierarchy of field staff at each location will be made at the discretion of the performer, with recommendations and concurrence from the BioWatch program. The staffing performer shall: Provide a Program Manager for the contract who will serve as the primary point of contact for the BioWatch Program and DHS Contracting Officer. Support planned and limited notice special events and surge operations (i.e., equipment deployment/demobilization, increased operations tempo, increased collection cycle, expanded array, etc.). Support changes to the static array (i.e., additions/reductions in number of collection sites) or collection routes. Accommodate appropriate and reasonable time off for personnel (i.e., paid time off, etc.) without compromising operations including special events and surge operations. title: Unison
description: The Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) is soliciting innovative proposals for Unison, a program to develop and evaluate collaborative-autonomy approaches that jointly adapt team decision-making and communications during mission execution. Unison will investigate approaches that enable autonomous teams to modify tactics, behaviors, coordination relationships, and information exchange as mission complexity and operational variability increase and communications become constrained and/or degraded (see Section 7, Glossary, for program-specific definitions of terms in italics). The core hypothesis of Unison is that a unified execution-time reasoning approach to action planning and communications planning can improve the effectiveness, scalability, and resilience of collaborative autonomy in dynamic, uncertain, and resource-constrained environments. Unison seeks to preserve mission performance while reducing communication dependence and bounding the reasoning burden imposed on individual agents. Unison frames collaborative autonomy as a multi-agent decision problem in which agents use local observations, mission context, relevance, and mission objectives to select a policy that jointly defines physical actions and communications actions. At each decision point, the team must determine what actions to take, which coordination relationships must be maintained, and what information must be exchanged to preserve the coordination required for mission success. Unison will investigate approaches across teams of tens to hundreds of agents operating in representative collaborative, multi-domain mission scenarios.

description: SOURCES SOUGHT / REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) MARKET RESEARCH FOR WOLF CREEK POWERHOUSE BRIDGE CRANE REHABILITATION DISCLAIMER: THIS IS A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) / SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE BEING RELEASED PURSUANT TO THE REVOLUTIONARY FEDERAL ACQUISITION REGULATION OVERHAUL (RFO) PART 10: MARKET RESEARCH. This RFI is issued solely for informational, market research, and planning purposes. It does not constitute an Invitation for Bid (IFB), Request for Quote (RFQ), or Request for Proposal (RFP), nor does it constitute a promise to issue an IFB, RFQ, or RFP in the future. No solicitation document exists at this time. Issuance of this notice does not constitute any obligation on the part of the Government and is not to be construed as a commitment by the Government, implied or otherwise, to issue a solicitation or award a contract. Respondents are advised that the United States Government will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this RFI. Proprietary information is not being requested, and respondents should refrain from submitting proprietary or business-sensitive data. Detailed technical specifications and drawings will only be made available upon issuance of a formal solicitation. 1. PURPOSE The Government is conducting this Sources Sought / RFI in support of market research to identify potential qualified and capable industry partners, including small businesses (Small Businesses, 8(a), HUBZone, Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Businesses [SDVOSB], and Women-Owned Small Businesses [WOSB]). The purpose of this notice is to gain knowledge regarding industry interest, capabilities, technical qualifications, and potential subcontracting arrangements to assist the Government in determining the appropriate acquisition strategy and competition basis. 2. PROJECT SCOPE OF WORK The contemplated requirement is for a firm-fixed-price standalone contract for the complete rehabilitation of the existing powerhouse bridge crane and incidental related work at the Wolf Creek Powerhouse in Jamestown, Kentucky. Crane Description: The existing powerhouse bridge crane is a 250-ton, top-running bridge type crane consisting of two bridge girders and two independent trolleys. Each existing trolley features: One (1) Main Hoist rated at 125 tons One (1) Auxiliary Hoist rated at 25 tons Major Work Items: The Contractor will be responsible for furnishing all labor, materials, supervision, engineering, tooling, and equipment required to complete the rehabilitation, which includes, but is not limited to, the following major items: Safety & Access: Modify personnel access and implement safety improvements to the bridge crane walkways, ladders, and maintenance platforms. Couplings & Seals: Replace hoist motor output shaft brake wheel coupling seals. Braking Systems: Replace hoist brake pads and perform comprehensive service to restore proper brake gap and operational torque. Gearboxes & Lubrication: Clean speed reducers (main hoist, auxiliary hoist, bridge drive, and trolley drive) and replace all lubricating oil; inspect and repair grease lubrication lines; replace main hoist open gear oil. Wheel & Axle Assemblies: Modify bridge and trolley wheel assemblies to replace original wheel bushings with new anti-friction roller bearings. (Note: The Contractor may have the option to replace entire wheel and axle assemblies or modify and reuse existing wheels and axles). Below-the-Hook Devices: Provide new, and perform non-destructive inspection, proof-load testing, and painting of below-the-hook lifting devices. Drives & Automation: Upgrade all variable frequency drives (VFDs) to Magnetek Series 5 VFDs (or approved system equal). Electrification & Grounding: Furnish and install a new fourth conductor bar dedicated as a continuous ground conductor; modify existing collectors to connect to the fourth conductor bar. Operator Cab & Controls: Provide and install a new ergonomic operator�s chair, wireless radio remote controllers, absolute hoist encoders, and high-efficiency LED bridge crane lights. Safety Instrumentation & Limits: Install load cell weighing devices and displays for both main and auxiliary hoists, along with new heavy-duty limit switches for bridge and trolley travel. Auxiliary Hoists: Furnish and install a new auxiliary tool hoist and a dedicated personnel rescue hoist. Testing & Commissioning: Perform full operational testing of all mechanical and electrical features of the crane, followed by 100% rated and 125% rated load tests in accordance with CMAA and OSHA requirements. Documentation: Develop and deliver a comprehensive new Operation and Maintenance (O&M) Manual integrating all legacy data from the existing manual with new equipment data to serve as a complete standalone guide. Blocks, Sheaves & Lifting Beams: Provide new main and auxiliary lower load block assemblies. Provide new main and auxiliary upper sheaves and pins. Provide new main hoist lifting beam, rotor lifting device, and turbine shaft lifting device. 15.Crane Runway Rails: Survey and modify existing runway crane rails to correct rail span, elevation, and straightness along the entire runway length. 3. title: BioWatch Program
description: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) SUMMARY: The Department of Homeland Security (DHS), FEMA, Office of Resilience, Chemical, Biological, Radiological, and Nuclear (CBRN) Support Directorate, requires support to staff identified local field offices and execute the daily BioWatch Program field operations in accordance with the attached Statement of Work (SOW). GENERAL INFORMATION: This RFI is issued solely for information gathering purposes to identify sources that can provide support for the BioWatch program field operations, special events and surge operations, and technology upgrades and integration. In accordance with FAR 15.101(c), RFIs may be used when the Government wants to obtain price, delivery, other market information, and capabilities for planning purposes. Responses to these RFIs are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. This RFI shall not be construed as a commitment by the Government for any purpose, nor does it restrict the Government to an ultimate acquisition approach. Respondents are solely responsible for all expenses associated with their RFI response. Respondents will not receive additional information in response to their submittal to the RFI and will not be notified of the resulting market research. INTRODUCTION: DHS�s mission is to safeguard the American people, the homeland, and American values with honor and integrity. In support of this mission, the FEMA works to prevent CBRN attacks against the United States by providing timely, responsive support to operational partners. The CBRN Support Directorate advances this mission through the BioWatch program, the nation�s only civilian program that monitors for aerosol releases of select bioterrorism agents. Since its establishment in 2003, BioWatch has maintained a bioterrorism air monitoring system that operates 24 hours a day, 7 days a week in large metropolitan areas, known as jurisdictions, and partnered with state and local public health communities to prepare for and respond to bioterrorist events. The BioWatch Program�s strategic objectives are to: Monitor for the highest-priority biological agents that could cause catastrophic outcomes. Protect the nation�s most at-risk locations. Maintain technical oversight of operations in close collaboration with state and local public health partners that execute the program. Conduct advanced development and use federal research and development (R&D) to procure and deploy improved detection capabilities at lower cost. Coordinate federal, state, and local public health preparedness activities to develop operational protocols for initiating response activities following the detection of an agent for which the system tests. Strengthen federal, state, and local stakeholder partnerships and improve operational efficiencies. To accomplish these objectives, each BioWatch jurisdiction maintains a static array of air samplers, the filters of which are collected daily by field operators. These filters are then delivered to a state or local operational laboratory where they are analyzed for select biological agents. Jurisdictions may also elect to surge operations by deploying additional units to monitor special events or increasing the collection cycle (e.g., twice a day collections). In addition, each jurisdiction has an advisory committee that coordinates with the BioWatch program on operations and biological event preparedness activities. At the federal level, the BioWatch program includes field, surge, laboratory, and biodefense preparedness operational components. Figure 1 depicts daily sample operations. Figure 1. BioWatch Sample Operational Process PURPOSE OF RFI Currently field operators and field-related tasks are not staffed by contract. The purpose of this RFI is to evaluate and determine the field staffing and support options for the BioWatch program to meet field operations requirements. The performer must enable the BioWatch program to maintain current field operations and continue to provide high quality, reliable, and timely delivery of field samples to the laboratories. In addition, due to its evolving operational needs, the performer must provide the necessary flexibility and adaptability to ensure BioWatch can address changes in sample collections for both planned events and unforeseen incidents, as well as assist with potential technology assessments, field evaluations, integration, and implementation. DESIRED CAPABILITIES FOR BIOWATCH FIELD STAFFING AND SUPPORT CAPABILITY Competent, proficient, and reliable field staffing is essential to ensure the BioWatch program continues to meet established requirements. In addition, the evolving threats and vulnerabilities that are identified at the state and local level require operational flexibility and adaptability that must be able to be supported with field staff capable of performing field operations and chain of custody in accordance with mission needs. A successful candidate staffing performer will provide field personnel to conduct BioWatch daily operations in select metropolitan cities within the United States. Composition and hierarchy of field staff at each location will be made at the discretion of the performer, with recommendations and concurrence from the BioWatch program. The staffing performer shall: Provide a Program Manager for the contract who will serve as the primary point of contact for the BioWatch Program and DHS Contracting Officer. Provide a primary point of contact, or lead, for each jurisdiction who will provide direct oversight of field staff and be responsible for administrative activities such as: Scheduling field staff and scoping collection routes. title: NETSAFA International Training Center Support
description: Amendment 3 Posted 11/24/2026, Step Two closing Date set to 4 December 2026 at 1200 EST. Amendment 2 posted 11/19/2026. Amendment 1 released on 11/4/2026 for Volume 1 Q and A responses. The Naval Education and Training Security Assistance Field Activity (NETSAFA), Pensacola, Florida, requires educational and training services, engineering and technical services, logistics, administration, management assistance, consulting and facilitation services, and transportation support services, training liaison, special mission personnel, and curriculum development. These services may be required in various locations in the U.S. or in foreign countries and may include support to foreign governments with formal and informal schools and courses, Mobile Training Teams (MTTs), and Mobile Education Teams (METs) under the auspices of the Security Cooperation Education Training Program (SCETP)/Security Assistance Training Program (SATP). The PSC code for this action is U099 Education/Training-Other associated with NAICS code 541330 under the Knowledge Based Services Taxonomy of services. NETSAFA supports international training in all warfare areas and at all levels of training for foreign countries. This is accomplished by staffing, operating, and managing international training support provided at NETSAFAs international training sites. The training sites are located in the NETASAFA International Training Center (NITC) located at Naval Air Station (NAS) Pensacola, Florida and NAS Whiting Field, Milton, Florida, and NITC Detachment Whiting Field, Milton, Florida. These sites are outfitted with computer training facilities, classrooms, and equipment needed to teach courses. They provide training and training support services in Navy activities such as government-owned contractor operating facilities. NETSAFAs international training sites are currently operational and have established curriculum. The training and other services required by this Performance Work Statement (PWS) are currently centered in four categories: General Training Programs, Aviation Training Programs, Mobile Training Teams (MTTs), and Mobile Education Teams (METs). Additionally, support will be required to meet emerging requirements in support of the SCETP/SATP. The instant requirement is for services associated with the international requirement of the United States and the foreign countries participating in the SCETP/SATP for a 12-month base period of performance beginning 01 March 2027 through 29 February 2028, with three (3) consecutive 12-month option periods pursuant to FAR 52.217-9, and a 6-month option period pursuant to FAR 52.217-8. The contractor will be required to periodically perform these services in various locations in the U.S. and may be required to perform these services in foreign countries. If support is needed in a foreign country, the contractor may be required to support foreign governments with formal and informal schools and courses, mobile training teams, and mobile education teams under the auspices of the Security Cooperation Education Training Program (SCETP) /Security Assistance Training Program (SATP).

description: The Naval Surface Warfare Center Philadelphia Division (NSWCPD) intends to negotiate and award a sole source Basic Ordering Agreement (BOA) to Argo Turboserve Corporation (ATC) as the only Authorized Distributor representing Curtiss Wright for OEM hardware components and support services for High Pressure (HP) and Low Pressure (LP) Propulsion Turbine Rotors and Propulsion Turbine and Ship Service Turbine Generator Overhaul Kits. description: This is a Notice of Intent, not a request for proposal. The National Institute of Health, Clinical Center (NIH-CC) intends to negotiate on an other than full and open competition basis with the following vendor: Luminex Corporation. Acquisition Description: The service agreement is for two FM3D instruments that are used by the HLA Lab for daily testing of transplant patients and donors. The instruments are utilized to provide low resolution HLA typing results for multiple protocols at the NIH. Several of these protocols are for transplants. The ELITE Service Plan provides the following coverage: � Unlimited visits for emergency repair (includes travel, parts and labor) � Two preventative maintenance visits per year � Priority scheduling for service requests � Certain software updates and modifications � Telephonic and online support 24 x 7 Response Time: On-site one business day response time for repair service. On-site arrival by end of next business day when dispatch determination is made by 6pm Central Standard Time (CST). This level of service and response is required by the HLA Lab to ensure the instruments are functioning properly. Any down time to an instrument can result in delayed testing turn-around time. Many of the patients who utilize the HLA Lab services are transplant patients and donors. Prompt testing is essential for the transplant protocols. The statutory authority for this sole source requirement is 41 U.S.C. 253(c) (1) as implemented by FAR 6.302-1 only one responsible source and no other supply of service will satisfy agency requirements. description: Scope This PWS defines the requirements for providing rotary wing flight services, supporting wildlifedamage management operations in Montana, including all tasks, deliverables, and standards required for safe and compliant flight operations. 2.2 - Background The United States Department of Agriculture (USDA), Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service (APHIS), Wildlife Services (WS) Program in Montana require contracted rotary wing flight services to support their wildlife damage management and related operational missions. The Contractor must furnish, operate and maintain fixed wing aircraft in accordance with the specifications. 2.3 - Purpose The purpose of this Performance Work Statement (PWS) is to identify the required tasks and responsibilities of the Contractor providing rotary wing flight services in support of the Montana WS Programs. The most probable causes of contamination are direct-connected manometers, mercury vacuum pumps, mercury seals, or the handling of mercury in the immediate vicinity. description: THIS REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) / SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE IS ISSUED SOLELY FOR INFORMATION AND PLANNING PURPOSES. THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION. SUBMISSION OF INFORMATION ABOUT PRICING, DELIVERY, THE MARKET, AND CAPABILITIES IS HIGHLY ENCOURAGED AND ALLOWED UNDER THIS RFI FOR PLANNING PURPOSES IN ACCORDANCE WITH (IAW) FAR 15.201(e). DISCLAIMER This RFI is issued solely for information and planning purposes and does not constitute a solicitation. All information received in response to this RFI that is marked as proprietary will be handled accordingly. IAW FAR 15.201(e), responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. Responders are solely responsible for all expenses associated with responding to this RFI. SOURCES SOUGHT/RFI DESCRIPTION This is NOT a solicitation announcement. This is a Sources Sought Notice / RFI only. The purpose of this Sources Sought Notice / RFI is to gain information about potential qualified sources and their size classification relative to NAICS 339112 (size standard of 1,000 Employees). Responses to this Sources Sought Notice / RFI will be used by the Government to make appropriate acquisition decisions. After review of the responses to this Sources Sought Notice / RFI, further RFIs and/or a solicitation or other announcements may be published. The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) is seeking sources capable of providing Bronchoscopy Simulator License & Processor that can address the attached list of DRAFT requirements for VA Long Beach Healthcare System. The list of DRAFT characteristics is intended to be descriptive, not restrictive, of the supplies/services that are required. If your company is interested in and capable of providing the required supplies/services, please provide the information indicated below. Response to this notice should include company name, address, point of contact, size of business pursuant to the following questions: (1) Submit your capabilities statement illustrating how your organization can/cannot meet the list of SALIENT CHARACTERISTICS requirements. For instances where your company cannot meet the SALIENT CHARACTERISTICS requirement(s), please explain. For instances where your company can meet the SALIENT CHARACTERISTICS requirement(s), please show how your company meets/exceeds each requirement. (2) Please review the list of SALIENT CHARACTERISTICS requirements and provide any additional feedback or suggestions. If none, please reply as N/A. (3) Please indicate the size status and representations of your business, such as but not limited to: Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB), Veteran-Owned Small Business (VOSB), HUBZone, Woman Owned Small Business (WOSB), Large Business, etc. (4) Is your company considered small under the NAICS code identified in this RFI? (5) Are you the manufacturer, authorized distributor, and/or can your company provide a solution to the required supplies/services described in the list of SALIENT CHARACTERISTICS? (6) If you are a large business, do you have any designated/authorized distributors? If so, please provide their company name, telephone, point of contact and size status (if available). (7) If you re a small business and you are an authorized distributor/reseller for the items identified above, do you alter; assemble; modify; the items requested in any way? If you do, state how and what is altered; assembled; modified. (8) Limitations on Subcontracting: How does your business ensure compliance with the limitations on subcontracting as outlined in 13 CFR § 125.6? (9) Are the items you are identifying/providing considered Commercial of the Shelf (COTS) items as defined in FAR Part 2.101 under commercial items? (10) Non-Manufacturer Rule: If applicable, can you confirm your business complies with the Non-Manufacturer rule? Specifically, does your company: Provide a product from a small business manufacturer or processor? Not exceed 500 employees? Primarily engage in the retail or wholesale trade and normally sell the type of item being supplied? Take ownership or possession of the item(s) with its personnel, equipment or facilities in a manner consistent with industry practice? (11) Please indicate whether your product conforms to the requirements of the Buy American Act? (12) What is your lead time to deliver a single unit with all components? Is there scale in lead time with greater quantities? Please elaborate. (13) What is estimated life span of your solution? What support/services does that entail? (14) Does your proposed equipment have FDA clearance? Please specify what FDA clearance(s) have been obtained. (15) Does your organization offer a leasing solution? Please elaborate. (16) Does your company have a Federal Supply Schedule (FSS) GSA/NAC/SAC/BPA/NASA SEWP or any other Federal Government contract? If so, please provide the contract number(s). (17) If you are an FSS GSA/NAC/SAC/BPA/NASA SEWP or any other Federal Government contract holder, are all the items/solutions you are providing information about available on your schedule/contract? Please state if all or some items are available on the contract. (18) General pricing of your products/solution is encouraged. Pricing will be used for the purpose of market research only. It will not be used to evaluate for any type of award. (19) Please provide your SAM.gov Unique Entity ID/Cage Code number. Responses to this notice shall be submitted via email to steven.crayton@va.gov. Telephone responses will not be accepted. Responses must be received no later than Friday December 4, 2026, by 12:00 PM CST. All responses to this Sources Sought/RFI will be used for planning purposes only. Responses to this Sources Sought Notice / RFI are not considered a request to be added to a prospective bidders list or to receive a copy of the solicitation. If further RFIs and/or a solicitation or other announcement is issued as a result of the information provided from this RFI, all interested parties must respond to the specific posting separately IAW the specifications of that announcement. Salient Characteristics The bronchoscopy simulator shall meet the following minimum salient characteristics: Simulation Hardware Components Shall include a replica video bronchoscope that connects to a desktop sensor module. Shall include a desktop sensor capable of registering insertion tube movement and translating those movements into a real-time, three-dimensional virtual airway environment. Shall include a dedicated laptop computer with integrated bronchoscopy simulation software. Training and Simulation Capabilities Shall provide comprehensive training for diagnostic bronchoscopy procedures through high-fidelity virtual reality simulation. Shall include a user-friendly interface with upper and lower airway training scenarios featuring normal and pathological anatomy. Shall provide objective performance metrics, scoring, session recording, playback functionality, and immediate user feedback for skills assessment and competency development. Shall support bronchoscope dexterity training, procedural skill development, maintenance of clinical proficiency, and exposure to multiple clinical scenarios prior to patient application. Shall enable safe and economical hands-on training through virtual simulation technology using a fully functional bronchoscope interface. Portability and System Requirements Shall be compact, lightweight, and portable, with a total system weight not to exceed 9 kg (19 lbs). Shall be capable of operating from the included laptop without requiring permanent installation or additional external equipment. Shall allow all system components to be stored and transported within a single carrying case. Shall be suitable for use in operating room environments, classrooms, training facilities, and conference settings.

title: Leadership Development Program Services
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Kansas City District (NWK), has a need for contractor services to develop, administer, and facilitate a part-time, yearlong Leadership Development Program (LDP) for up to 12 competitively selected, mid-career employees. The contractor shall provide program and curriculum development; formal leadership and management classroom instruction; diagnostic and assessment tools; facilitation of orientation, retreats, and other LDP activities; development of Individual Leadership Development Plans; participant feedback and program evaluations; and related program-administration support. The requirement also includes a separately priced option for the design, coordination, and delivery of targeted leadership-training sessions for specified NWK leadership groups. The objective is to develop participants� leadership and management competencies and prepare a pool of high-potential leaders for future USACE and NWK leadership positions.

description: The purpose of amendment 0002 is to incorporate the following documents to solicitation FA300227RDSS4:Combined Synopsis Solicitation DSS IV, dated 18 Nov 26 // Attachment 1 - PWS DSS IV, dated 20 Nov 26 // Attachment 2 - Addenda to RFO 52.212-1 Instructions to Offerors, dated 18 Nov 26 // Attachment 3 - Addenda to RFO 52.212-2 Evaluation Criteria, dated 18 Nov 26 // Attachment 6 - DSS IV Pricing Matrix Spreadsheet, dated 18 Nov 26----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------The purpose of this requirement is to maintain and support PTT device solutions based on state- of-the-art commercial simulation environments, hardware solutions for the cockpit simulation environment, and ancillary software elements. The Government has the right to modify the quantity of devices/locations pending contract modification and funding. The Contractor shall maintain a common software interface to integrate current and future PTT software and hardware components as required by program goals, hardware solutions for the cockpit simulation environment, and on-premises network and data architecture hardware and support, as appropriate for deployed training systems.

title: Replacement TAO Wind Monitors for the National Data Buoy Center at Stennis Space Center, MS
description: The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration�s (NOAA) Acquisition and Grants Office, Eastern Acquisition Division-Kansas City intends to negotiate and award a purchase order, on a sole source basis, under authority of RFO FAR 6.103-1, with RM Young Company for Replacement TAO Wind Monitors (P/N 05103-1) to be delivered to National Data Buoy Center at Stennis Space Center, MS. The sole source determination is based on NOAA�s only one source is capable rationale. The RM Young propeller wind monitors technology uses magnetic induction for measuring wind speed which requires no energy input. Essentially you get the wind speed for free with respect to power requirements. Further, the directional portion of the sensor only requires 0.6 mW of power. That is 100 times less power requirement than an ultrasonic anemometer. This low power wind measurement is imperative in a battery-operated remote buoy station. The propeller anemometer also provides for the measurement of wind gusts over 100 m/s where no ultrasonic anemometer technology can currently measure in that range. The NDBC helped develop the R.M. Young propeller anemometer which is now considered the industry standard. No other propeller anemometer available has the reliability of the R.M. Young propeller anemometer. Hence, the R.M. Young model 05103-1 anemometer was selected as the anemometer for the TAO refresh system in 2010 and the TAP Recapitalization effort in 2023. The NDBC now has a complete TAO network populated with these 015103-1 wind monitors and this procurement replaces those units lost at sea, damaged beyond repair, or have reached their end of life during fiscal years 2025 and 2026. The RM Young 05103-1 is provided with the cable and connector required to match current TAO cabling. The 05103-1 also provides a pulse output for wind speed as a result of the magnetic induction technique for the measurement. The selection of another manufacturer�s wind sensors could result in $100K of engineering efforts to rework the hardware and firmware of the TAO system and the NDBC wind tunnel testing equipment to accept different connections and output formats. Further, due to TAOs climate study the new sensor would need to be tested side-by-side the RM Young 05103-1 for a year to develop the transition equation to ensure there are no step or abrupt changes in the general wind speed and direction trends. This year long side-by-side testing could cost more than $100k as it would require a co-located buoy at several locations. This pre-solicitation notice is not a request for competitive proposals and no solicitation package is available. However, firms that believe they can fully meet the government�s requirements may submit substantiating documentation or a request for additional information in writing to Abigail Green at Abigail.green@noaa.gov within 15 days after publication of this pre-solicitation notice. Such requests and documentation will be evaluated solely for the purpose of determining whether or not to conduct this procurement on a competitive basis. A determination by the government not to conduct a competitive procurement, based upon responses to this notice, is solely within the discretion of the government. Oral communications are not acceptable in response to this pre-solicitation notice.

title: Enterprise Workspace Management Support
description: THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE ONLY. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS. THIS SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE IS PUBLISHED FOR MARKET RESEARCH PURPOSES ONLY. This notice is issued by the Department of the Navy, Naval Sea Systems Command (NAVSEA HQ), on behalf of NAVSEA Facilities (Enterprise Workspace Management). NAVSEA is comprised of Headquarters (HQ) activities located at the Washington Navy Yard (WNY) and technical/industrial field organizations across more than 40 geographically dispersed activities spanning over 34 million gross square feet of facilities and supporting approximately 80,200 personnel. NAVSEA Facilities seeks to identify potential sources interested in and capable of fulfilling the requirements for enterprise workspace management support services to implement, sustain, expand, configure, and improve the ARCHIBUS Workplace Management System (IWMS) / Computer-Aided Facility Management (CAFM) platform. The current baseline utilizes ARCHIBUS version 25.2 (and approved upgrades) hosted across staging, testing, training, and production environments by the Enterprise Digital Capabilities (EDC) team at NSWC Dahlgren, VA. The requirement encompasses NAVSEA HQ, Program Executive Offices (PEOs), and participating field activities, including Naval Warfare Centers (NSWC/NUWC), Naval Shipyards (Norfolk, Pearl Harbor, Portsmouth, Puget Sound), Regional Maintenance Centers (CNRMC, MARMC, SERMC, SWRMC), Supervisors of Shipbuilding (SUPSHIP Bath, Groton, Gulf Coast, Newport News), and related naval commands. (Incumbent Contract Reference: Currently satisfied under SeaPort Task Order N00178-14-D-8048-EH01 by BlueWater Federal Solutions, Inc. Estimated LOE is approximately 240,910 Direct Labor Hours over a 5-year period of performance: one 12-month base year plus four 12-month option years). This requirement may include the following efforts: Provide full lifecycle day-to-day ARCHIBUS system administration, user account lifecycles, security groups, Virtual Private Archives (VPAs), user roles, dashboard design, workflows, and Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs). Execute field-activity site rollout plans using Agile processes to incorporate stakeholder requirements, assess site constraints, deploy licensed modules, and deliver formal Site Rollout Completion Packages. Maintain capacity to execute rollouts at up to five (5) field activities simultaneously when surge capacity is required. Establish and validate data integrity, GeoHierarchies, and organizational structures linking personnel, room/cubicle space, telecommunications, and IT hardware assets. Perform authorized interior and exterior LiDAR/3D laser scanning, building feature surveys, and facility asset verification in accordance with Government CAD/BIM standards (e.g., USACE CAD Standards). Execute CAD polylining, drawing conversion, layer standardizations, and Building Information Modeling (BIM) publishing and integration into ARCHIBUS. Provide robust prime-contractor quality control, oversight, and deliverable validation for any subcontractor-performed survey, scanning, or CAD/BIM efforts prior to Government submission. Develop, test, and sustain automated daily data feeds between source systems, legacy databases, and the ARCHIBUS production database hosted in the Enterprise Digital Capabilities (EDC) environment. Prepare, package, and document Configuration Change Requests (CCRs), staging test scripts, release notes, user-impact assessments, and rollback plans, supporting testing and deployment from Navy Marine Corps Intranet (NMCI) client environments. Facilitate stakeholder alignment sessions, business process mapping, and change-readiness activities across enterprise leadership and field activity commands. Develop role-based training curriculums, interactive guides, quick-reference aids, and SOPs; conduct hands-on training within the dedicated ARCHIBUS training environment prior to local go-live events. Accomplish full operational transition within a six (6) week phase-in period post-award, maintaining an Integrated Master Schedule (IMS), Quality Control Plan (QCP), and structured risk/issue registers. Ensure all personnel are U.S. citizens possessing a favorably adjudicated Federal Background Investigation at the Tier 3 (T3) level for Common Access Card (CAC) credentials and Navy IT network access. Maintain an adequate cost accounting system approved by DCAA/DCMA (FAR 16.301-3 / SF 1408) to support a CPFF task order.

description: THIS IS A PRE-SOLCITATION NOTICE. THIS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL OR INVITATION FOR BID. The US Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Detroit District is seeking contractors with the capability to provide construction services for the St. Marys River Sea Lamprey Trap (SLT) project. This project consists of construction of a sea lamprey trap structure downstream of Gate 16 of the St. Marys River Compensating Works in Chippewa County, MI. The project will involve installing a steel grating platform, trap vault, and lift system. The steel-grating platform will be 11-feet-long and 8-feet-wide and be supported by steel members fixed to a concrete wingwall. The trap vault will be composed of steel plates and fixed to the required platform and the existing concrete sill. The lift system will include one free-standing jib crane with a minimum rating of 1 ton. Demobilize when complete. NO SOLICITATION, SPECIFICATIONS, OR DRAWINGS are available for this Notice. title: HYDROSPHERE, BIOSPHERE, & GEOPHYSICS (HBG) SUPPORT SERVICES II - FINAL REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL (FRFP)
description: The National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA), Goddard Space Flight Center (GSFC), hereby invites interested parties to review the Final Request for Proposal (FRFP) for the Hydrosphere, Biosphere, and Geophysics (HBG) Support Services II requirement supporting the Earth Sciences Division (ESD) at NASA/GSFC. The principal purpose of this requirement is to provide science research that conceives, develops, and applies space, field-deployed (i.e. airborne and in situ) and laboratory based technologies and observations to address issues of importance to society. These include but are not limited to water resources, land and ocean ecosystems, global and regional sea level change, changes in the Earth�s cryosphere, gravity field, magnetic field, solid Earth, and the terrestrial reference frame. The Statement of Work, Attachment A, describes the scope of the requirement. This contract is for support of a full range of science and research activities across the breadth of the various Laboratories that make up the HBG sub-division: the Cryospheric Sciences, Ocean Ecology, Hydrological Sciences, Biospheric Sciences, and Geodesy and Geophysics Laboratories. This contract is also for support of science, research and computing activities within the Terrestrial Information Systems Laboratory (TISL), also in the ESD. For the purposes of this document and contract the term HBG will be used to encompass all the Laboratories of the HBG sub-division and the TISL. NASA will conduct this acquisition as a small business set-aside. This competitive acquisition was originally contemplated as a Cost-Plus-Fixed-Fee (CPFF), Indefinite-Delivery/Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) contract with the ability to issue CPFF task orders. Following further acquisition planning and assessment of the Government's requirements, the contract structure has been modified. The HBG II Draft Request for Proposal (DRFP) posted on April 8, 2025 was issued as an IDIQ CPFF solicitation. As amended, this competitive acquisition will now result in a HYBRID Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) with the ability to issue Cost Plus Fixed Fee (CPFF) AND Firm- Fixed Price (FFP) task orders. The contract will have an effective ordering period of five years from the contract effective date. Interested offerors are encouraged to review the solicitation and all associated attachments for complete details regarding the requirements and proposal submission instructions. Please see the attached cover letter for additional information.
