title: NOTICE OF INTENT TO SOLICIT FROM A SINGLE SOURCE - Environmental Modeling Technical Support and EEMS Workshop Jacksonville Harbor Deepening Project
description: NOTICE OF INTENT TO SOLICIT FROM A SINGLE SOURCE Environmental Modeling Technical Support and EEMS Workshop Jacksonville Harbor Deepening Project Proposed Source: DSI, LLC | UEI: MBMESK928KP3 The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Jacksonville District, intends to solicit and award a firm-fixed-price contract to DSI, LLC, on a single-source basis pursuant to Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) RFO 6.302-1 Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements. This notice is issued to inform industry of the Government�s intent and to invite capability statements from firms that believe they can meet the requirement. This is not a request for quotations or proposals; no solicitation is available at this time. The requirement supports the Jacksonville Harbor Deepening Project�s environmental modeling activities, including assessment of salinity conditions in the Lower St. Johns River. The anticipated period of performance is 12 months. The required services include: � Preparation of customized workshop materials using the Government�s existing Jacksonville Harbor modeling files and relevant assessment scenarios; � One five-day, instructor-led, hands-on workshop for Government personnel covering the current EFDC+ Explorer Modeling System (EEMS), including EFDC+, EFDC+ Explorer, and Grid+, as applied to model configuration, calibration, validation, salinity analysis, scenario evaluation, post-processing, and interpretation of results; and � Up to 50 hours of follow-on remote technical assistance and troubleshooting relating to the existing EEMS modeling workflow. The acquisition does not include purchase of a perpetual EEMS software license or three years of software maintenance. DSI has represented that it developed and solely owns EEMS and maintains the source code for EFDC+, EFDC+ Explorer, and Grid+. DSI further represents that knowledge of current-release features, workflows, and model options depends on its recent software development work; that it provides customized training and technical support directly to U.S. clients; and that it has no licensed or authorized U.S. distributors, resellers, or agents. Based on the Government�s current technical assessment and market research, USACE anticipates that DSI is the only source reasonably available to provide the required current-release, developer-level training and technical assistance. The Government will consider information submitted in response to this notice before making a final acquisition decision. Interested responsible sources may submit a written capability statement demonstrating their ability to meet the complete requirement. Responses should specifically address current-release EEMS expertise; the ability to provide project-specific, hands-on training and follow-on troubleshooting for EFDC+, EFDC+ Explorer, and Grid+; access to the technical knowledge needed to support the current release without reliance on DSI; relevant experience; and the proposed approach and timeframe for performance. General environmental modeling experience or familiarity with earlier software versions, without evidence of capability to meet the stated current-release requirements, may not establish the ability to perform this requirement. Submit capability statements electronically to Ligaya Lowe, Contract Specialist, at ligaya.m.lowe@usace.army.mil, with a copy to Gerald Garvey, Contracting Officer, at gerald.l.garvey@usace.army.mil, no later than the response deadline stated above. Include the firm�s legal name, UEI, point of contact, and a concise description of relevant capabilities. Telephone responses will not be accepted. All timely responses will be reviewed solely to determine whether a competitive acquisition approach is appropriate. A determination not to complete this proposed acquisition, based on responses to this notice, is within the Government�s discretion and will be documented in the acquisition file. The Government is not obligated to issue a solicitation or reimburse any costs incurred in responding to this notice.

title: HYDROSPHERE, BIOSPHERE, & GEOPHYSICS (HBG) SUPPORT SERVICES II - FINAL REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL (FRFP)
description: UPDATE #1 � Amendment #0001 to the RFP was released on October 22, 2026. UPDATE #2 � Amendment #0002 to the RFP was released on October 26, 2026. The National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA), Goddard Space Flight Center (GSFC), hereby invites interested parties to review the Final Request for Proposal (FRFP) for the Hydrosphere, Biosphere, and Geophysics (HBG) Support Services II requirement supporting the Earth Sciences Division (ESD) at NASA/GSFC. The principal purpose of this requirement is to provide science research that conceives, develops, and applies space, field-deployed (i.e. airborne and in situ) and laboratory based technologies and observations to address issues of importance to society. These include but are not limited to water resources, land and ocean ecosystems, global and regional sea level change, changes in the Earth�s cryosphere, gravity field, magnetic field, solid Earth, and the terrestrial reference frame. The Statement of Work, Attachment A, describes the scope of the requirement. This contract is for support of a full range of science and research activities across the breadth of the various Laboratories that make up the HBG sub-division: the Cryospheric Sciences, Ocean Ecology, Hydrological Sciences, Biospheric Sciences, and Geodesy and Geophysics Laboratories. This contract is also for support of science, research and computing activities within the Terrestrial Information Systems Laboratory (TISL), also in the ESD. For the purposes of this document and contract the term HBG will be used to encompass all the Laboratories of the HBG sub-division and the TISL. NASA will conduct this acquisition as a small business set-aside. This competitive acquisition was originally contemplated as a Cost-Plus-Fixed-Fee (CPFF), Indefinite-Delivery/Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) contract with the ability to issue CPFF task orders. Following further acquisition planning and assessment of the Government's requirements, the contract structure has been modified. The HBG II Draft Request for Proposal (DRFP) posted on April 8, 2025 was issued as an IDIQ CPFF solicitation. As amended, this competitive acquisition will now result in a HYBRID Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) with the ability to issue Cost Plus Fixed Fee (CPFF) AND Firm- Fixed Price (FFP) task orders. The contract will have an effective ordering period of five years from the contract effective date. Interested offerors are encouraged to review the solicitation and all associated attachments for complete details regarding the requirements and proposal submission instructions. Please see the attached cover letter for additional information.

title: NOTICE OF INTENT TO SOLICIT FROM A SINGLE SOURCE - Environmental Modeling Technical Support and EEMS Workshop Jacksonville Harbor Deepening Project
description: NOTICE OF INTENT TO SOLICIT FROM A SINGLE SOURCE Environmental Modeling Technical Support and EEMS Workshop Jacksonville Harbor Deepening Project Proposed Source: DSI, LLC | UEI: MBMESK928KP3 The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Jacksonville District, intends to solicit and award a firm-fixed-price contract to DSI, LLC, on a single-source basis pursuant to Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) 12.102(a). Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements. This notice is issued to inform industry of the Government�s intent and to invite capability statements from firms that believe they can meet the requirement. This is not a request for quotations or proposals; no solicitation is available at this time. The requirement supports the Jacksonville Harbor Deepening Project�s environmental modeling activities, including assessment of salinity conditions in the Lower St. Johns River. The anticipated period of performance is 12 months. The required services include: � Preparation of customized workshop materials using the Government�s existing Jacksonville Harbor modeling files and relevant assessment scenarios; � One five-day, instructor-led, hands-on workshop for Government personnel covering the current EFDC+ Explorer Modeling System (EEMS), including EFDC+, EFDC+ Explorer, and Grid+, as applied to model configuration, calibration, validation, salinity analysis, scenario evaluation, post-processing, and interpretation of results; and � Up to 50 hours of follow-on remote technical assistance and troubleshooting relating to the existing EEMS modeling workflow. The acquisition does not include purchase of a perpetual EEMS software license or three years of software maintenance. DSI has represented that it developed and solely owns EEMS and maintains the source code for EFDC+, EFDC+ Explorer, and Grid+. DSI further represents that knowledge of current-release features, workflows, and model options depends on its recent software development work; that it provides customized training and technical support directly to U.S. clients; and that it has no licensed or authorized U.S. distributors, resellers, or agents. Based on the Government�s current technical assessment and market research, USACE anticipates that DSI is the only source reasonably available to provide the required current-release, developer-level training and technical assistance. The Government will consider information submitted in response to this notice before making a final acquisition decision. Interested responsible sources may submit a written capability statement demonstrating their ability to meet the complete requirement. Responses should specifically address current-release EEMS expertise; the ability to provide project-specific, hands-on training and follow-on troubleshooting for EFDC+, EFDC+ Explorer, and Grid+; access to the technical knowledge needed to support the current release without reliance on DSI; relevant experience; and the proposed approach and timeframe for performance. General environmental modeling experience or familiarity with earlier software versions, without evidence of capability to meet the stated current-release requirements, may not establish the ability to perform this requirement. Submit capability statements electronically to Ligaya Lowe, Contract Specialist, at ligaya.m.lowe@usace.army.mil, with a copy to Gerald Garvey, Contracting Officer, at gerald.l.garvey@usace.army.mil, no later than the response deadline stated above. Include the firm�s legal name, UEI, point of contact, and a concise description of relevant capabilities. Telephone responses will not be accepted. All timely responses will be reviewed solely to determine whether a competitive acquisition approach is appropriate. A determination not to complete this proposed acquisition, based on responses to this notice, is within the Government�s discretion and will be documented in the acquisition file. The Government is not obligated to issue a solicitation or reimburse any costs incurred in responding to this notice.

title: MH-60 Airborne Mine Countermeasure (AMCM) Carriage, Stream, Tow and Recovery System (CSTRS) Obsolescence Support
description: Introduction The Naval Air Systems Command (NAVAIR), in support of PMA-299 MH-60 Multi-Mission Helicopter Program Office, is seeking sources to support the Airborne Mine Countermeasure (AMCM) Carriage, Stream, Tow and Recovery System (CSTRS). The Contractor shall have the capability, experience, equipment, and facilities required to support ongoing obsolescence issues affecting CSTRS. Program Background AMCM was originally contracted in 2000 and executed in the DoD RDT&E funding under H2773, under which the first CSTRS prototypes were delivered to the U.S. Government. Carriage, Stream, Tow, and Recovery System (CSTRS) is part of the Airborne Mine Countermeasures (AMCM) weapons systems used on the MH-60S aircraft to allow the mounting, deployment, and recovery of Airborne Mine Neutralization System (AMNS) and Airborne Laser Mine Detection System (ALMDS). The Government requires mitigation strategies to address obsolescence issues within the AMCM CSTRS Mission Kit in support of the following: Provide sustainment support, system updates, and technical reach back for the existing AMCM CSTRS Mission Kits to combat rising obsolescence issues within the associated Weapons Replaceable Assemblies (WRAs) and Shop Replaceable Assemblies (SRAs). Proposed mitigation strategies and solutions shall be backwards compatible with all U.S. Navy MH-60S AMCM versions to include: � CSTRS Non-Tow Mission Kit part number 04101A01-03 � CSTRS Tow Mission Kit part number 09412 � CSTRS Base Mission Kit part number 09754A01-00 The Contractor shall design and implement solutions to address obsolete WRAs and SRAs, as appropriate, to facilitate improved logistical support for the AMCM CSTRS Mission Kit. The AMCM Mission Kit is comprised of the CSTRS Base Mission Kit, CSTRS Base Structure Assembly, Tow Mission Kit, and the Non-Tow Mission Kit. The Contractor shall provide form, fit, and function replacements as possible solutions to facilitate maintaining inventory without requiring replacement of currently fleeted WRAs/SRAs. The Contractor shall support aircraft testing, deliver a full Technical Data Package for all upgraded parts, deliver an Engineering Change Proposal (ECP) for incorporation into the current system configuration, and update all applicable logistical support data. The Contractor shall ensure solutions comply with AMCM System Specification 233A172, or a superseding specification revision approved by the Government, if made available prior to any contract award. Required Capabilities 1. Design solutions shall comply with the requirements of the MH-60S Airborne Mine Countermeasures (AMCM) System Specification, document number 233A172 Rev J, dated February 16, 2015, or its superseding Government-approved revision, whichever is available at potential contract award. This shall include all aspects of design, qualification, and testing of solutions. 2. Design solutions shall be backward compatible at the WRA/SRA level to AMCM CSTRS Mission Kit. 3. Design solutions shall provide the ability to support software growth capability for potential new software-driven modifications for the AMCM Winch Maintenance Laptop Software (WMLS). 4. Software updates, if needed, shall be backward compatible with current AMCM CSTRS Mission Kit configuration hardware and operating system. 5. Design solutions shall adhere to current U.S. Department of War cybersecurity requirements. 6. Provision of life cycle estimates for new components. 7. Provide documentation verifying solutions, when integrated into CSTRS, are safe for flight in support of U.S. Navy flight clearance processes. 8. Provide on-site and remote support to Government-conducted testing of final solutions. 9. Deliver to Government Level III Technical Data Packages for design solutions for this effort. Submission Information It is requested that interested businesses submit to the contracting office a brief capabilities statement package, no more than 12 pages in length, single-spaced, with a minimum 12-point font, demonstrating the ability to perform the tasks listed under Required Capabilities. This documentation must address, at a minimum, the following: 1. Company name; company address; company business size; and point-of-contact name, phone number, fax number, and email address. 2. Company profile, including number of employees, annual revenue history, office location(s), Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) number, and a statement regarding current small/large business status. 3. Prior/current corporate experience performing efforts of similar size and scope to the tasking described under Required Capabilities within the last three years, including contract numbers, contract values, Government point of contact with current telephone number, and a brief description of how the referenced contract related to those tasks. 4. Management approach to staffing this effort with qualified personnel. 5. Statement regarding capability to obtain the required industrial security clearances for personnel. 6. Company ability to begin performance upon contract award. 7. What type of work the company has performed in the past in support of the same or similar requirement. 8. Whether the company can or has managed a task of this nature; if so, provide details. 9. Whether the company can or has managed a team of subcontractors before; if so, cite contracts and teaming arrangement. 10. Specific technical skills the company possesses that ensure capability to perform the tasks. 11. If a small business, an explanation of the company�s ability to perform at least 50 percent of the tasking described in Required Capabilities. 12. Statement including current small/large business status and company profile, including number of employees, annual revenue history, office location, CAGE code, UEI number, etc. 13. Whether the respondent is a large business or qualifies as a Small, Small Disadvantaged, Small Disadvantaged Veteran-Owned Small Business, Women-Owned, 8(a), HUBZone, or Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business Concern. 14. Ability to meet requirements in the Facility and Safeguarding requirements. Responses to this Sources Sought, including any capabilities statement, shall be electronically submitted via email to eric.j.richey.mil@us.navy.mil, in either Microsoft Word or Portable Document Format (PDF). All data received in response to this Sources Sought that is marked or designated as corporate or proprietary will be protected. Information and materials submitted in response to this request will not be returned. Classified material shall not be submitted. No phone calls will be accepted. All questions must be submitted via email. The Government is not committed or obligated to pay for the information provided, and no basis for claims against the Government shall arise as a result of a response to this Sources Sought. The updated PMT PID for this opportunity is N00019-26-RFPREQ-APM299-0678.

title: Fuels Management Services at Malmstrom Air Force Base, MT and FE Warren Air Force Base, WY
description: Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) Energy is issuing a Request for Proposal (RFP) for fuels operations and management to include bulk storage services, retail service station support, alongside aircraft services, and entire fuels management services at two Government-Owned, Contractor-Operated (GOCO) facilities, Malmstrom Air Force Base (AFB), MT and FE Warren AFB, WY. The Contractor will ensure safe, accurate, and timely handling, quality control, and accountability of all Defense-Wide Working Capital Fund (DWCF)-owned petroleum products under their control. The Contractor will perform required maintenance to ensure facilities, associated systems, vehicles, and equipment remain operational to meet the base mission. The Contractor shall provide sufficient general-purpose vehicles with appropriate capability to meet the contract requirements but not limited to escorting fuel deliveries where required, towing bowsers, transporting personnel, and performing expeditor duties as needed. The Contractor should provide sufficient special purpose vehicles with appropriate capability to meet the contract requirements for aviation and ground product services. The Contractor will comply with environmental protection, safety, and security directives. The Contractor will conduct required training to ensure personnel are fully qualified to perform Performance Work Statements (PWS) tasks. Tasks identified in the PWS are performed by either the Contractor or Agency as specified in Appendix M The Contractor is responsible for staffing, operations, maintenance, safety, security, environmental protection, training, contractor-furnished items, and Contractor Detailed Plans related to the fuel operations at the location. The Contractor shall conduct all necessary fuels operations to support base operations, airshows and special events, deployments, exercises, and contingencies under normal conditions, as well as, during periods of heightened security, inclement weather, or other unique situations. Operations must be safely and efficiently conducted to receive, store, transfer, issue, and account for fuel products with appropriate controls to ensure fuel quality, inventory accuracy, and no environmental impact. The Contractor shall operate and maintain the self-service automated service station facilities, equipment, and systems and ensure sufficient product is available to provide 24 hours a day, seven days a week support of ground fuels. The Contractor shall perform required tasks to ensure fuel is properly accounted for and issued to only authorized users. This procurement will be 100% restricted to Service Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) participation. Firms submitting a proposal under this RFP must be certified as SDVOSB by the Small Business Administration in accordance with FAR 19.1403. The NAICS Code is 493190 (Other Warehouse and Storage). The Government anticipates awarding two firm fixed-price contracts. This requirement will be for a four-year base period (April 1, 2027 to March 31, 2031), a five-year option period (April 1, 2031 to March 31, 2036), and an option to extend the contract for up to six individual months (April 1, 2036 to September 30, 2036). This procurement will be solicited under full and open competition after exclusion of sources. Interested firms may submit proposals for one location or both locations. The solicitation will be published electronically on the SAM website at https://sam.gov/. Interested companies responding to the solicitation will be required to register in the System for Award Management (SAM) and Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE) prior to submitting a proposal. The Date of the Pre-Preproposal conference, in conjunction with the sites visit will be listed in the solicitation. Offerors will be required to submit in writing to the Contract Specialist (via e-mail) the name(s) and email(s) of the individual(s) who plan to attend by 11:00 AM Eastern Time on October 22, 2026.

title: FY27 Electronics and IED Neutralization Course
description: 1. Introduction & Purpose: The 900th Contracting Battalion (MICC - Fort Bragg, NC) is conducting market research to identify capable sources, specifically looking for Small Businesses (including 8(a), SDVOSB, WOSB, and HUBZone firms) capable of providing a comprehensive, tactical Electronics and IED Neutralization Course in support of the 28th Ordnance Company (EOD). This is a Sources Sought Notice only and does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP) or Request for Quotation (RFQ). The government will use responses to this notice to determine the appropriate acquisition strategy, specifically whether a socio-economic set-aside is warranted. 2. Core Requirements Summary: The contractor shall provide all personnel, training aids, equipment, facilities, and supervision necessary to execute three (3) five-day courses for up to twelve (12) personnel per iteration (totaling 36 personnel). Key Training Modules: Basic electronics theory, circuit breadboarding, diagnostic tools, and microcontrollers. Advanced hand-entry/defeat techniques under specialized conditions (e.g., Night Vision Goggles / blackout precautions). Improvised Explosive Device (IED) switch diagnostics, radiography, and post-blast diagnostics. Instructor Qualifications: Lead instructors must possess verifiable DoD Special Mission Unit (SMU) EOD operational experience within the last ten (10) years. Facility & Storage Requirements: Dedicated electronics/practical lab workspace to support 12 personnel. Scenario-based tactical training lanes (e.g., multi-building villages or search environments). A secure storage facility of at least 400 sq. ft. for Government Furnished Equipment (GFE) (including NVGs and organic EOD kit) compliant with AR 190-11 (Physical Security of Weapons, Ammunition, and Explosives). Place of Performance: Contractor facility must be located within a 5-hour driving radius of Fort Bragg, NC. Logistics & Accommodations: Government-Furnished: Transportation, student lodging, and meals will be provided by the Government. The contractor is only responsible for training facilities and instruction. 3. Capability Statement Submission Requirements: Interested firms must submit a Capability Statement (not to exceed 5 pages) demonstrating their ability to perform this requirement. Submissions must include: A. Company Profile: Company Name, Address, and Website. Unique Entity ID (UEI) and CAGE Code. Business Size/Socio-Economic Status under NAICS 611699 (e.g., SDVOSB, 8(a), Small Business). B. Technical Capability & Experience: SMU EOD Cadre: Describe your organization's access to and ability to field instructors possessing the required DoD Special Mission Unit (SMU) EOD experience. Facility & Equipment Storage: Describe your facilities, including the practical electronics lab space and tactical scenario lanes. Confirm that your secure storage facility complies with AR 190-11 physical security guidelines. Geographic Radius: Confirm the physical location of the training facility and that it meets the 5-hour driving radius requirement from Fort Bragg, NC. C. Past Performance Provide up to three (3) examples of similar tactical training or advanced EOD/IED electronics instruction performed within the past five (5) years, including contract number, agency/customer, dollar value, and a brief description of the work. Please submit all capability statements electronically in PDF format to SFC Cameron R. Wade (Contracting Officer) at cameron.r.wade.mil@army.mil no later than 04 December 2026 at 1500 EST. Please reference "Sources Sought: FY27 Electronics and IED Neutralization" in the subject line of your email.

description: 1. Introduction & Purpose: The 900th Contracting Battalion (MICC - Fort Bragg, NC) is conducting market research to identify capable sources, specifically looking for Small Businesses (including 8(a), SDVOSB, WOSB, and HUBZone firms) capable of providing a comprehensive, tactical Advanced Marksmanship and Close Quarters Battle (CQB) Course in support of the 28th Ordnance Company (EOD). title: FIID Advanced Anti-Fraud and Risk-Modeling Proof of Concept
description: FEMA�s Fraud Investigations and Inspections Division (FIID), in coordination with the Office of the Chief Component Procurement Officer (OCCPO), is conducting market research to identify commercially available advanced anti-fraud and entity-risk modeling solutions for a potential competitive, multi-vendor Proof of Concept (POC). The POC would assess vendors� ability to identify potentially high-risk business entities using authorized data sources, fraud-risk indicators, and analytical methods, including artificial intelligence, machine learning, predictive analytics, rules engines, entity resolution, anomaly detection, graph and network analytics, identity and business verification, and optical character recognition. FEMA seeks scalable solutions that accurately identify potential risk while minimizing false positives and false negatives; provide transparent, reviewable explanations for alerts, risk scores, and entity assessments; integrate with cloud, hybrid, API-based, and batch-processing government environments; and support applicable federal security, privacy, accessibility, records-management, and data-governance requirements. The POC would be limited to evaluating technical capabilities and would not include live operational screening, grant eligibility determinations, adverse-action recommendations, or decisions affecting an individual�s or entity�s rights, benefits, eligibility, or safety. 1. title: Request for Proposals (RFP) for Fresh Fruit & Vegetable support for DLA Troop Support's DoW Troop and Non-DoW School and Indian Tribal Organization customers located in Dallas, TX
description: The DLA Troop Support intends to solicit a full-line of produce support for DoD (Troop) customers and Non-DoD (USDA School & Indian Tribal Organization) customers located in the Dallas, Texas Zone. This acquisition will be issued on a small business set-aside (100%) basis. A waiver of the Non-Manufacturer rule has not been requested for this acquisition because it is an acquisition for multiple items. In accordance with 13 CFR 121.406(d)(1), if at least 50% of the estimated contract value of an acquisition for multiple items is composed of items that are manufactured by small business concerns, then a waiver of the Non-Manufacturer rule is not required. As such, for this acquisition, it is expected that items comprising at least 50% of the contract value will be manufactured by small business concerns. The contracting officer must be immediately notified if it appears as though this requirement will not be met. The total length of the contract will be five (5) years. It contains one (1) twenty-four (24) month tier, and two (2) eighteen (18) month tiers. Its estimated maximum total contract dollar value is $243,976,437.00. The delivery points require indefinite quantities of Fresh Fruit and Vegetables throughout the term of the contract. A more detailed listing of the delivery sites can be found in the solicitation. All responsible sources may submit proposals that will be considered by DLA Troop Support. The Government will award a contract(s) resulting from this solicitation to the responsible offeror(s) whose offer(s) conforming to the solicitation will be most advantageous to the Government, price and other factors considered. The source selection method for this procurement will be the Lowest Price Technically Acceptable (LPTA) source selection procedures and shall use the following to evaluate offers: 1. Technical Acceptability - A technically acceptable offer is an offer that takes no exceptions to the terms and conditions in the solicitation and complies fully with all submission requirements, including submissions relating to the two subfactors listed below. A proposal that takes exception to solicitation terms and conditions or that fails to comply with all submission requirements may be deemed technically unacceptable and, thus, may be found ineligible, and removed from further consideration for the award. By submitting a proposal with no exceptions, an offeror is confirming it possesses the necessary facilities, equipment, technical skills and capacity to successfully provide all items required by this solicitation. The following sub-factors will be evaluated and must be found acceptable for a proposal to be eligible for award: A. Perishable Agricultural Commodities Act (PACA) License - The offeror shall possess and submit proof of a valid current PACA license. B. USDA Harmonized Good Agricultural Practices (GAP) Plus + Standard Audit with warehouse and food defense addenda and/or USDA Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP) audit - The Contracting Officer will require an offeror to submit a valid USDA Harmonized GAP Plus + Standard audit, including addenda for warehouse and food defense, and/or USDA GMP audit, or an independent third-party certifying company audit report(s) / certificate for each place of performance identified in the offeror's proposal. The audit report(s) must demonstrate a passing score in the following parts: General, Warehouse and Food Defense addenda. In lieu of a USDA Harmonized GAP Plus + Standard and/or USDA GMP audit report / certificate, the offeror may submit an audit report / certificate conducted by a recognized private independent third-party certifying company certifying to an industry recognized food safety standard that exceeds all aspects of the USDA Harmonized GAP Plus + Standard audit and/or USDA GMP report / certificate requirements. Offerors relying on a non-USDA Harmonized GAP Plus + Standard and/or USDA GMP audit report / certificate that do not agree to have a USDA Harmonized GAP Plus + Standard and/or USDA GMP audit report / certificate for each place of performance prior to the start of contract performance will be found technically unacceptable. 2. Pricing - Pricing is required for all items found in the Schedule of Items (for Group 1 and 2 (2a and 2b), if applicable) and for all tiers. Failure to offer pricing for all items and for all tiers may result in a proposal being removed from consideration for award as technically unacceptable. The Government will perform an aggregate price analysis on all items found in the Schedule of Items (for Group 1 and 2 (2a and 2b), if applicable). To determine an offeror's Evaluated Aggregate Price for Group 1, the Weighted Aggregate Distribution Price will be added to the Aggregate Delivered Price. To determine an offeror's Evaluated Aggregate Price Group 2 (2a and 2b), the Weighted Aggregate Distribution Price will be added to the Aggregate Delivered Price for each sub-group 2a and 2b, respectively, to come to a preliminary Evaluated Aggregate Price for each sub-group. Then, the preliminary Evaluated Aggregate price for 2a and 2b will be added together to determine the offeror's Evaluated Aggregate Price for Group 2. Please refer to paragraph (d) below for further details regarding these price components. The award(s) will be made on the basis of the lowest Evaluated Aggregate Price (for each group) of proposals meeting or exceeding the acceptability standards for non-price factors. The Government reserves the right to remove item(s) from the Schedule of Items. Prior to award, the offered prices of the presumptive awardee(s) will be evaluated on an individual line-item basis to determine whether each price is fair and reasonable using analytical techniques deemed appropriate by the Contracting Officer in her/his complete discretion. A. Price Components: 1. Weighted Aggregate Distribution Price: Aggregate Distribution Price is obtained by first multiplying the proposed distribution price for each item in the Schedule of Items by the item's estimated quantity to calculate the total distribution price for each item. Then, the total distribution prices of all items will be added together to determine the total distribution price for tier 1. The total distribution price for each subsequent tier will also be calculated. The total distribution prices for all tiers will be added together to determine the Aggregate Distribution Price. The Aggregate Distribution Price is then multiplied by a weighting factor of 6 to arrive at the Weighted Aggregate Distribution Price. Note: the weighting factor is applied only to the overall Aggregate Distribution Price (not on a line item basis), and is to be used for evaluation purposes only. The Government's use of a weighting factor of 6 for distribution pricing is done in order to more accurately balance the significance of the pricing components and their respective impact on any subsequent contract(s) issued under this solicitation. 2. Aggregate Delivered Price: The Aggregate Delivered Price is obtained by first multiplying the proposed delivered price of each item in the Schedule of Items by the item's estimated quantity to calculate the total delivered price for each item. Then, the total delivered prices of all items will be added together to determine the total delivered price for tier 1. The total delivered price for each subsequent tier will also be calculated. The total delivered prices for all tiers will be added together to determine the Aggregate Delivered Price. 3. Evaluated Aggregate Price: The Evaluated Aggregate Price is obtained by adding the Weighted Aggregate Distribution Price and Aggregate Delivered Price together. 4. For purposes of the Price Proposal Evaluation, Weighted Aggregate Distribution Price and Aggregate Delivered Price are considered equal. This equality is accounted for mathematically by applying a weighting factor of 6 (based on current Government data) to the Aggregate Distribution Price. Option

title: MSHA Approved Portable, Inflatable Refuge Alternative
description: * BE ADVISED THIS IS FOR INFORMATIONAL PURPOSES ONLY, AND NO QUOTES SHOULD BE SUBMITTED* To mirror current industry standards, the inflatable refuge alternative device must meet the MSHA requirements for use in Underground Coal mines. This device must support the over 54� seam MSHA space requirements. The training devices will represent the currently approved US devices with one coming from Chembio and one coming from Strata. The vendor must deliver two fully equipped, portable inflatable refuge alternative trainers (one trainer from Stata/one trainer from Chembio) and one fully equipped portable, inflatable refuge alternative from either manufacturer. description: Page 7 of 7 REQUEST FOR INFORMATION THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION. The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) Veterans Health Administration (VHA) is issuing this Request for Information (RFI) as market research to determine the availability of vendors that can provide a Veteran Transportation Software Solution (Vetride) with VHA enterprise-wide licensing that includes all requirements identified in the attached Draft Performance Work Statement (PWS). This RFI constitutes neither a Request for Quote (RFQ), Request for Proposal (RFP), nor a guarantee that one will be issued by the Government in the future; furthermore, it does not commit the Government to contract for any services described herein. The VA is not, at this time, seeking proposals or quotes, and therefore, will not accept, review, or evaluate unsolicited proposals or quotes received in response hereto. This notice is not to be construed as a commitment on the part of the Government to award a contract, nor does the Government intend to pay for any information submitted because of this request. The Government does not reimburse respondents for any costs associated with submission of the information being requested or reimburse expenses incurred for responses to this RFI. The information provided may be used by VA in developing its acquisition strategy Product Description (PD) or PWS. Any information submitted by respondents to this RFI is strictly voluntary. Interested parties are responsible for adequately marking proprietary, restricted, or competition sensitive information contained in their response. This is a request for information and does not obligate the Government in any way, nor does it commit the Government to any specific course of action. Product information, brochures, part numbers, and/or other description information may be included with the submission. This notice is issued solely for information and planning purposes. No funds have been authorized, appropriated, or received for this effort. BACKGROUND The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Veterans Health Administration (VHA), and Member Services (MS) Veterans Transportation Program (VTP) require the VetRide Transportation Solution, which provides scheduling software, routing systems, invoice processing for contracted and non-contracted vendors, and hardware deployment across VA medical centers. The solution delivers integrated transportation capabilities including vehicle, passenger, clinic, and Beneficiary Travel (BT) eligibility, dynamic and automated routing and scheduling, and comprehensive reporting. It supports decentralized operations in which each VA medical center manages transportation for Veterans in its service area and offers reimbursement for medically related travel. REQUEST FOR INFORMATION In response to this RFI, VA seeks to gain industry feedback on the DRAFT Performance Work Statement (PWS). Please respond with suggested approaches/recommendations to the attached PWS, Vendor Questions, and RFI Respondent Information. Responses should not exceed 10 pages, single-spaced standard 1-inch margins and in a 12-point font. Responses to this RFI shall be submitted via email, with filename - Vetride.solution.rfi-name of your company - to William.Freer@va.gov, Debra.Clayton2@va.gov no later than December 4, 2026 at 3 PM EDT. VENDOR QUESTIONS Describe your solution s ability to meet all the requirements set forth in the attached Draft PWS. � Please specifically address the following requirements: Ability to Interface with multiple VA and non-VA portals. Ability to deliver a Cloud Based solution that can be integrated with both Android and Apple IOS systems. 2. How would user access be managed for your services and is it possible that specific VA users would be provided a direct ability to grant or remove user access? � � 3. Describe your technical support capabilities and what kind of help desk/customer services your solution provides. � � 4. Provide a Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) estimate to include pricing models that would be most advantageous to the Government. � � 5. Describe your pricing methodology. Is there a price per user unit price? Do you offer an enterprise license? Do you offer tiered pricing methodology? � Do you offer the ability to choose different products, vice all included ? � � 6.� Has the draft PWS provided sufficient detail to describe the technical requirements that encompass the services to be performed under this effort?� � ______ YES _______ NO (if No, answer question below)� If NO , please provide your technical comments/recommendations on elements of the draft PWS that may contribute to a more accurate proposal submission and efficient, cost effective effort.� RFI RESPONDENT INFORMATION Vendors shall provide the following information: Name of Company Address Point of Contact Phone Number Email address CAGE Unique Entity Identifier Number Company Business Size and Status for NAICS NAICS code(s) applicable to the products and services you can provide Any contract vehicle of which you are part that can be used to acquire your products/services. Typical contract vehicles include General Services Administration contracts, National Aeronautics and Space Administration Solutions for Enterprise-Wide Procurement VI, or other Government-Wide Acquisition Contracts. Please also include Contract Number, expiration date, and point of contact. Socioeconomic data: If a small business, what type of small business are you? Are you able to comply with federal acquisition regulations clause 52.219-14, Limitations on Subcontracting in execution of this effort? Are you able to comply with 852.219-75, VA Notice of Limitations on Subcontracting Certificate of Compliance for Services and Construction and with subcontracting limitations in accordance with 13 CFR 125.6 in execution of this effort? This information will assist in determining whether a set aside may be appropriate for this effort. As part of market research, after RFI responses are received and reviewed, VA may contact you for additional information.

title: TEAR DOWN, TEST & EVALUATION (T&E) AND REPAIR OF THE TEST SET, FUEL CONTROL SYSTEM, (NSN 4920-99-551-5371) (PART NUMBER (P/N) TTU-597/E)
description: The Naval Air Warfare Center, Aircraft Division (NAWCAD) Lakehurst, NJ intends to negotiate on a sole source basis with ULTRA ELECTRONICS ICE INC, (CAGE: 5Y111), for the issuance of a Purchase Order (PO). The designated contractor, ULTRA ELECTRONICS ICE INC, shall provide to the Naval Air Warfare Center Aircraft Division (NAWCAD) Lakehurst the material and services necessary for the TEAR DOWN, TEST & EVALUATION (T&E) AND REPAIR OF THE TEST SET, FUEL CONTROL SYSTEM, (NSN 4920-99-551-5371)(PART NUMBER (P/N) TTU-597/E) ULTRA ELECTRONICS ICE INC (CAGE 5Y111) is the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) and hold the proprietary rights to the drawings, specifications, and data necessary to the Fuel Control Test Set (P/N BC849A6010-000). Therefore, they are the only source capable of the tear down, test & evaluate, and repair of the Fuel Control Test Set (P/N BC849A6010-000). The Government intends to solicit and negotiate this requirement under the authority of 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1), Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements.
